question: What is the official website?
expected_data_source: PB_PATIALA_WASTE_SOLID_WASTE (has a live portal) vs PB_MOHALI_WASTE_SOLID_WASTE (PDF only)
expected_information: Depends entirely on which city: Patiala has a real live portal (Punjab Grievance Redressal System, https://connect.punjab.gov.in/) captured in complaint_channel; Mohali's only captured URL is the source citizen-charter PDF itself, not a separate live grievance website (Mohali's real toll-free/app channels ARE captured, just not as a 'website' URL).
notes: A correct answer must not claim a live website exists for every city just because one city has one -- must be looked up per-record, never assumed to generalize.

question: Where can I download the application form?

notes: Re-confirmed from the earlier citizen-service-questions audit (CSQ_DOC_02) -- still true, not re-fabricated.

question: Street light not working.
service: Street light repair -- no location given at all
expected_data_source: AMBIGUOUS -- 3 VERIFIED cities + 28 SYNTHETIC cities all have a STREETLIGHTS record; none can be selected without a location
expected_information: The correct behavior is to ask the citizen which city/area they're in (per the requested Ask JanMitra behavior) rather than guessing or defaulting to any one city's figures.
verification_requirement: N/A -- location resolution required before retrieval
notes: Tests that the system does not silently pick e.g. Odisha's 10-day figure as a generic answer when no location was given -- there is no 'default city'.

question: Street light not working in Punjab.
service: Street light repair -- state given, city not given
expected_data_source: AMBIGUOUS -- both PB_MOHALI_STREETLIGHTS_REPAIR and PB_PATIALA_STREETLIGHTS_REPAIR match 'Punjab' and have genuinely different figures (10 days vs 2 days respectively)
expected_information: Still needs city-level disambiguation -- Mohali and Patiala's own figures differ, so a state-level answer would have to either ask which city or present both, not silently pick one.
notes: State alone resolves to more than one VERIFIED record with different figures -- this is a genuine ambiguity in the data, not a gap, and must be surfaced as such.

question: Street light not working in Mohali.
expected_information: Uniquely resolves to one VERIFIED record -- fully answerable.
notes: City-level is the finest granularity any RAG record in this data set actually supports (see TYPEAB_LOC_WARD_EN below).

question: Street light not working in Ward 3, Mohali.
expected_data_source: PB_MOHALI_STREETLIGHTS_REPAIR (city-level only -- no ward-level RAG record exists)
expected_information: The RAG knowledge base has ZERO records with `ward` populated (0/126, confirmed by direct field inspection) -- asking with ward-level specificity provides no additional precision over city-level in the current data. IMPORTANT: this is a different system from the app's own location-hierarchy database tables (states/districts/.../wards), which DO have real ward data for 6 cities including Mohali -- but that table is not linked to the RAG knowledge base's own state/district/city text fields. A correct answer should give Mohali's city-level figures and must NOT claim ward-specific precision it doesn't have.
notes: Important architectural gap to flag: RAG location granularity currently tops out at city level regardless of how precisely a question is asked.

question: Street light not working near Sector 68, Mohali.
expected_information: Same limitation as TYPEAB_LOC_WARD_EN -- no locality/area field is populated on any RAG record.
notes: Locality-level precision does not exist in the RAG data set for any of the 126 records, verified/synthetic alike.

question: [Use current location] Street light not working near me.
service: Street light repair -- resolved via GPS
expected_data_source: Depends on LocationResolver.resolve_coordinates() output -- if it resolves to a city with a KnowledgeRecord, same as TYPEAB_LOC_CITY_ONLY_EN; otherwise UNANSWERABLE
expected_information: This is an APPLICATION-LAYER concern, not a RAG concern: the GPS pipeline (backend/services/location_resolver.py) resolves coordinates to state/district/city (never ward/locality, see its module docstring), and that resolved city name would need to be matched against the RAG data set's own (denormalized, not linked) city field -- a matching step that does not exist yet in any RAG code. Currently, GPS resolution and RAG retrieval are two entirely separate systems with no integration between them.
notes: Flagging a real, current architectural gap: the location-resolver's output has no wired path into RAG retrieval -- both systems exist and work independently, but nothing connects them yet. This is expected for this phase (retrieval/RAG integration is explicitly out of scope) but should not be assumed solved.

question: Street light not working in Atlantis.
expected_information: No VERIFIED or SYNTHETIC record exists for this place (it doesn't exist). The correct behavior is to say clearly that no information is available for this location -- NEVER to fall back to a different city's figures and present them as if they applied here.
notes: The critical hallucination-prevention test case: an invalid/unrecognized location must produce an honest 'no data' response, not a plausible-sounding fabricated one borrowed from a real city.
